MARKING CRITERIA (out of 5):
5 marks: Explains skilfully the ways the interview and images convey the effect that memories can have on us over time using detailed, well-chosen supporting evidence
4 marks: Explains effectively the ways the interview and images convey the effect that memories can have on us over time using well-chosen supporting evidence
3 marks: Explains the ways the interview and images convey the effect that memories can have on us over time using some supporting evidence
2 marks: Describes how the interview and/or images convey relevant idea(s)
1 marks: Provides some relevant information about the text

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Panebianco’s interview and images convey the ways photos have the capacity to capture and evoke our memories and connect us with our past. She conveys this by bringing her family’s memories to life by placing her father’s slides of the past into moments of her ‘everyday life’. She holds up the images from the past in front of present-day locations and takes new photos to blur ‘the lines between past and present’. The metaphor of blurred lines, and the layered images emphasise the ways Panebianco has been able to bring memories of the past into the present and connect with her family’s history including, ‘weddings, road trips, family and relationship moments’. The interview and images also convey the importance of printing photos in order to be able to connect with the past and sustain ‘family traditions’ over time.
